judged_text: The new catch block returns calendarReference?.map(...) ?? [], which is an empty array for any error thrown before calendarReference is assigned (e.g., the newBookingId lookup at the top of the try). A prisma/DB failure during reschedule now resolves to an empty result list that callers treat as 'no calendar references to update', so the reschedule completes in the database without any calendar update and without the success:false failure entry the old catch returned — the failure signal is gone.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts`, `calendarReference` is initialized as `PartialReference[] | undefined = undefined` before the `try`. In the new `catch`, it returns `Promise.resolve(calendarReference?.map(...) ?? ([] as Array<EventResult<NewCalendarEventType>>))`. If an error is thrown before `calendarReference` is assigned (e.g., during the early `prisma.booking.findUnique` / `newBookingId` lookup at the top of the `try`), `calendarReference` remains `undefined` and the function resolves to `[]` rather than returning a `success:false` failure entry as the previous implementation did. This change can silently drop the failure signal on DB/prisma errors.
